proof_summary: Rewrite the quantity as \(a(n)=2\sigma(n)-B(n)\), where \(B(n)=\sum_{d\mid n}\sigma(d)\); multiplicativity and the formulas \(\sigma(2^k)=2^{k+1}-1\), \(B(2^k)=2^{k+2}-k-3\), \(\sigma(p)=p+1\), and \(B(p)=p+2\) for primes are then applied to the pairwise coprime factors of \(N=2^{14}\cdot4409\cdot458009\). Since \(4409\) and \(458009\) are prime, this gives \(2\sigma(N)=132367152569400\) and \(B(N)=132367152569399\), hence \(a(N)=1\), while \(N=33085221781504\) is neither \(1\) nor \(12\).
